components.html: <button class="ds-sign">Start trail <svg width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M4 12h15M13 6l6 6-6 6"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-sign { display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:10px; width:100%; max-width:420px; min-height:66px; padding:12px 46px 12px 22px; border:0; cursor:pointer; font:400 1.65rem/1 'Lilita One', 'Arial Rounded MT Bold', sans-serif; letter-spacing:.02em; color:#2a1100; background:#ff7a1a; clip-path: polygon(0 0, calc(100% - 30px) 0, 100% 50%, calc(100% - 30px) 100%, 0 100%); transition: transform .15s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1); } .ds-sign:hover { transform: translateX(4px); } .ds-sign:active { transform: translate(2px,3px); } .ds-sign:focus-visible { outline:4px solid #ff7a1a; outline-offset:3px; }

components.name: Plank

components.css: .ds-markers { display:flex; align-items:center; max-width:360px; margin:0 auto; } .ds-markers i { flex:1 1 0; height:6px; background:repeating-linear-gradient(90deg,#ff7a1a 0 10px,transparent 10px 16px); } .ds-markers b { flex:0 0 auto; width:22px; height:22px; border-radius:50%; background:#f3faea; border:3px solid #12301d; } .ds-markers b.ds-now { width:30px; height:30px; background:#ff7a1a; box-shadow:0 0 0 6px rgba(255,122,26,.3); animation: ds-here 1.4s ease-in-out infinite; } @keyframes ds-here { 50% { box-shadow:0 0 0 11px rgba(255,122,26,.12); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-markers b.ds-now { animation:none; } } .ds-mcap { text-align:center; font:600 .9rem Lexend, system-ui, sans-serif; color:#1f4329; margin:8px 0 0; }

narrative.overview:
Every screen is a stretch of trail through a hand-drawn forest map. The ground is moss green carrying topographic contour lines; wayfinding is built from the things you find on a real waymarked walk: an orange dashed trail, circular waymarker discs, routed timber posts, and arrow-ended plank signs with yellow routed lettering. Reading matter sits on pale map-legend sheets edged in forest ink. Nothing floats on a gradient and nothing is a generic rounded card; every container is either a piece of timber, a legend sheet, or the map itself.

The density is low and the targets are large, because the app is read from a distance by a child who is mid-movement. Type does the shouting (Lilita One, set like routed sign lettering) while Lexend carries the reading. Colour has a job: orange means "go this way", yellow lettering means "this is a sign", each creature lives in its own zone colour, and forest ink holds every edge. The world is the same on the parent landing page; there the map is the hero and the trailhead sign is the primary action.

Motion belongs to the trail: the path draws itself, posts pop up from their base, the campfire flickers, and the "you are here" marker breathes. All of it stops under reduced motion, where the trail renders fully drawn.
keyCharacteristics: Moss map ground with irregular contour lines, never a flat or gradient background.
Timber (wood grain plus a routed lip) for every wayfinding control; legend sheets for every block of reading.
Arrow-ended signs point the way forward; back signs point left.
Six fixed creature zone colours, used for zones, discs and nothing else.
Original, code-authored SVG only: discs, map, Cub, icons, faces.
Big targets (46px minimum, 64–104px for primary trail controls).

rules.name: The Orange Means Go Rule
rules.body: Trail Orange is reserved for the route and the next action. A decorative orange fill elsewhere dilutes the one signal a child follows.

rules.name: The Zone Belongs to the Creature Rule
rules.body: Zone colours appear only on a creature's zone and disc. They never become general UI accents, and a creature never appears on another creature's colour.

rules.name: The Never Colour Alone Rule
rules.body: Every colour-coded meaning also carries a word, a shape or a position: answer signs have labels, stars have an aria label, markers have a "Post 1 of 3 · round 1 of 2" caption.

rules.name: The Lettering Is Routed Rule
rules.body: Display text is always Lilita One at weight 400 in sentence or title case with a slight positive tracking (0.005–0.02em). No uppercase transforms, no faux bold.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Lilita One labels and names things; Lexend explains them. A paragraph is never set in Lilita One.

rules.name: The Lying Flat Rule
rules.body: Shadows always fall downward and stay soft and short. Nothing glows, and no surface floats higher than a modal.

rules.name: The Point the Way Rule
rules.body: Only controls that move the child somewhere take the arrow silhouette. A setting, a toggle or a reading panel is never an arrow.

dos: Do put every screen on the moss ground with contour lines, and frame the forest map with a 4px forest-ink border at 22px radius.
Do use the arrow sign for the one forward action on a screen, in Trail Orange, full width, at least 66px tall.
Do set wayfinding labels in Lilita One Sign Yellow on timber, and reading text in Lexend on a legend sheet.
Do keep every tap target at 46px or more, and primary trail controls at 64px or more.
Do give every colour-coded state a word or shape as well (answer labels, star aria labels, marker captions).
Do draw any new art as original SVG in code, outlined in forest ink, in the same flat-fill style as the discs and the Cub.
Do stop all trail motion under `prefers-reduced-motion` and show the end state (trail drawn, dashes visible, no confetti).
donts: Don't build screens from rounded cards on a gradient; containers are timber, legend sheets or the map.
Don't use a zone colour for anything except its own creature's zone and disc.
Don't use Trail Orange as decoration; it is the route and the next action.
Don't add emoji or icon-font icons; icons are the drawn 2.5px-stroke set.
Don't add stock or AI-generated raster images; every shipping image is SVG authored in `app.js` (exported to `img/*.svg`).
Don't set display text in uppercase or in a system face; Lilita One at 400 only.
Don't show points shops, streak counters, leaderboards or anything that can go down; visible progress only grows.
